meta.description: Published illumination and Earth-visibility results for named points and regions at the lunar south pole (well-lit ridges and rims). Values are study results for the stated height and period, not results for our own dates.
meta.coordinate_convention: Decimal degrees; latitude south negative; longitude east-positive, lon_east_180 (-180..180) and lon_east_360 (0..360). Sources publish 0-360 E (or West for Bussey 2010); the -180..180 form was computed during conversion (lon - 360).
meta.validation: Copied from research notes of 2026-11-14. Not validated by the science lead. Do not label any point permanently sunlit; recompute sunlight for the exact point, height and dates.
source_meta_notes: Values copied from research notes of 2026-11-14; not independently validated.

'avg_illumination_pct' = time-average of the visible fraction of the solar disc; 'solar_visibility_pct' = fraction of time any part of the Sun is visible. These are different metrics. Some sources (Glaeser 2014, Mazarico) report 'time sunlit'; this is flagged in metric_note.

Studies disagree by 10-25 points with DEM resolution and metric: 240-474 m DEMs overestimate (smoothing of near-field topography); 100 m WAC imagery underestimates (lit strips <100 m not resolved, 1 year only); 20 m / 5 m LOLA values lie between. Researcher's recommendation: treat 240-474 m percentages as upper bounds and 100 m image-based as lower bounds.

Paywalled papers (Mazarico 2011 Table 3, Speyerer and Robinson 2013, Glaeser 2014, Wueller 2025/2026, De Rosa 2012) were NOT opened; their numbers come from abstracts, tables reproduced in later papers, or search-result excerpts, as flagged per item.

Barker 2021 values are conservative percentiles over 100 Monte Carlo DEM clones (1st percentile for illumination and LCIP, 99th percentile for LCSP). RoI positions are given only as south-polar stereographic X/Y km; lat/lon were NOT computed here.
Per-site Earth-visibility percentages for Shackleton rim, Connecting Ridge, de Gerlache rim, Nobile rim and Haworth from a primary source were not obtained.
longest_dark_h is in hours where the source gives hours; other units are in longest_dark_text.
